text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics loosens ties with its German subsidiary Grundig. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell is to invest in the construction and management of power stations. (p1)
- Spanish media continue to vent their anger at Dutch finance minister Gerrit Zalm, whom they see as "Bundesbank messenger". (p1)
- Former disposable cutlery plant De Ster owner Joost Ritman, fighting to gain back his firm, loses court case against ING bank. (p1)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT takes over Belgian packager Van Mierlo Proost. (p3)
- Tank storage and distribution concern Pakhoed is to buy 50 pct stake in two French chemical distributors belonging to the Gazechim group. (p3)
- Small and medium-sized businesses association MKB complains to economic affairs ministry about bank tariffs for smart card payments transactions. (p3)
- Food and detergent group Unilever to sell its professional microbiology activities to venture capital company Cinven. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Consumers organisation calls PTT telecom's rate hike for telephone numbers information from 66 to 95 cents absurd. (p2)
- Leading Dutch executives give cabinet the thumbs-up. (p2)
- Rotterdam-based container transshipment firm ECT books flat 1996 net on slightly lower turnover. (p31)
- U.S. concern IAMS Petfood to build new plant for European market in Coevorden. (p31)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma promises concerns of Rotterdam port that trucks will no longer be hindered by traffic jams in a few years. (p1)
- Arithmetician Ben Roelen accuses automation company Cap Gemini of stealing his solution for the year 2000 problem in computers. (p19)
- Dutch export association NEC seriously concerned about five percent drop in exports to Asia and South America. (p19)
- Chemicals concern Akzo-Nobel's 1996 results will be as forecast. (p21)
TROUW
- Dutch environmental minister Magaretha de Boer is trying to construct a distribution code for EU environment policy. (p9)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Heineken brewery to boost production in Burundi despite international embargo. (p10)
- Employers in Rotterdam port concerned about conflict between central planning bureau CPB and harbour authority GHR on port's expansion. (p10)
